title: Update-half parity with lore-cli LCLI-593: not-run reasons, Codex detail by progress, and an update-timeout override
description: QCLI-371 AC4 update-half parity read, 2026-09-26, against lore-cli LCLI-593 (opum-ai/lore-cli#297, merged 46133fc0, an ancestor of lore-cli dev), files src/core/agent-plugins.ts and src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts read by ref. The core mechanism MATCHES quest: the update runs only when installed and the runtime is named; Claude is scoped; Codex runs marketplace upgrade then add; update/updateOk/updateDetail; a failed update keeps its remedy; nothing is ever installed or enabled. lore is AHEAD in three observable ways. (1) Every not-run report carries updateDetail naming why: no runtime named (and the --target command that would), disabled (never enabled), not-installed (never installed), or unreadable. quest not-run reports carry no updateDetail. (2) The Codex detail is worded by how far the update got, via an outcome.completed step count. The all-plugins CODEX_MARKETPLACE_NOTICE is appended only when the marketplace upgrade succeeded; when the upgrade succeeded and the re-add failed, the detail says the marketplace-wide refresh already happened (ruling 25: say the side effect where it happens). quest has one fixed success sentence and on a partial failure says only the failure. (3) LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS overrides the 600s per-step update deadline, separately from the list deadline. Also structural, not observable: lorePluginUpdateSteps is the single source for both the argv run and the command printed. The unnamable-scope defect is filed separately, as a ruling violation.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every update not-run report carries an updateDetail whose text matches lore-cli 46133fc0 notRunDetail with lore agents --target/--force replaced by quest agents --update-instructions --target

The Codex update detail follows lore-cli codexUpdateDetail: the all-plugins notice only after the marketplace upgrade succeeded, and the already-refreshed wording when the re-add then fails; tests cover upgrade-fails, add-fails and both-succeed
QUEST_AGENT_PLUGINS_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS overrides the per-step update deadline independently of the list deadline
One function yields both the update argv and the printed update command; bun run check exits 0; cited against lore-cli 46133fc0

plan: 1. src/domain/agent-plugins.ts gains AgentRuntime (ports re-exports it), the plugin id and marketplace names, plainScope, and questPluginUpdateSteps(runtime, scope), the ONE source of the argv the adapter runs and the command the report prints (lore lorePluginUpdateSteps at 46133fc0); a managed or unnamable claude scope yields no steps.
2. The port update(runtime, scope) runs those steps and returns {ok, detail, completed}; success detail is the steps joined with &&, as lore.

3. Every not-run report carries lore notRunDetail text, with the lore command swapped for quest agents --update-instructions --target and the CLI self-name swapped (ruled on QCLI-383); managed stays first.
4. codexUpdateDetail by progress with the Codex marketplace notice, plugin names swapped.
5. QUEST_AGENT_PLUGINS_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS in composition, parsed as the list override.
6. Tests: upgrade-fails, add-fails, both-succeed; each not-run reason; timeout override; mutation-check; bun run check.
implementationNotes: IMPLEMENTED against lore-cli 46133fc0 (LCLI-593, #297), with its managed ordering from e6d504f6. (AC1) Every not-run report carries updateDetail from notRunDetail: managed first (ruling 28, LCLI-608), then the bare call "this call named no runtime, so it updates none; `quest agents --update-instructions --target <runtime>` updates this one", then the disabled, not-installed and could-not-be-read texts, with "lore agents" swapped for "quest agents" (the CLI self-name swap ruled on QCLI-383). The unnamable-scope detail (QCLI-383) is unchanged. (AC2) The Codex update outcome now carries completed, the count of steps that exited 0. codexUpdateDetail follows lore: the all-plugins notice only after the upgrade succeeded, and the already-refreshed wording when the re-add then fails. The notice is pinned against lore text with the plugin names swapped; this replaces the old quest-only success prose. (AC3) QUEST_AGENT_PLUGINS_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS sets the per-step update deadline in composition and is parsed like the list override; a test proves the list override does not shorten it. (AC4) questPluginUpdateSteps in src/domain/agent-plugins.ts is the ONE source of the argv the adapter runs and the command printed. Tests prove a failed update prints exactly the argv that ran, for claude and for codex. The port update signature is now (runtime, scope). EVIDENCE: 12 new cases. Three targeted mutations each reddened exactly the predicted set: no not-run detail reddened the 4 reason cases; Codex detail ignoring progress reddened both-succeed and add-fails, while upgrade-fails stayed green; ignoring the update env var reddened the deadline case. bun run check: 721 pass, 1 fail. The failure is test/e2e/release/candidate-bundle "a bundle records whether it carries the committed bytes": it passes on a clean tree and on this tree with --timeout 60000, and takes 8-10s wall against a 5s timeout at load average 27.6, so it is load, not this change; CI decides.

GATE: re-run on the tree rebased onto origin/dev 88974c1: bun run check exit 0, 722 pass, 0 fail. The candidate-bundle test passed once load average fell from 27.9 to 9.0, which confirms the earlier failure was load.
finalSummary: The update half of agents --update-instructions now matches lore-cli LCLI-593 (46133fc0). Every not-run report carries an updateDetail from lore notRunDetail (managed first, then bare call, disabled, not-installed, unreadable), with the command and the CLI self-name swapped. The Codex detail is worded by progress: the marketplace notice only after the upgrade succeeded, and the already-refreshed wording when the re-add fails. QUEST_AGENT_PLUGINS_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS overrides the per-step update deadline independently of the list deadline. questPluginUpdateSteps (src/domain) is the single source of the argv run and the command printed. Verified with 12 call-logging cases, three targeted mutations that each reddened exactly the predicted set, and bun run check exit 0 (722 pass).
